subject: Geography
description: Cropping seasons, leading producer states, MSP, Green Revolution, recent farm laws

questions.stem: India's THREE main cropping seasons are:
questions.explanation: KHARIF — sown June-July (with monsoon), harvested Oct-Nov. Crops: rice, maize, jowar, bajra, ragi, soybean, cotton, groundnut. RABI — sown Oct-Nov (winter), harvested March-April. Crops: wheat, barley, mustard, gram, peas, oats. ZAID — short summer season (March-June). Crops: watermelon, cucumber, fodder. Names from Urdu/Arabic — Kharif = autumn harvest, Rabi = spring harvest. India's agricultural calendar still revolves around these three.

questions.stem: India's largest producer state of WHEAT is:
questions.explanation: UP — largest wheat producer (~33-34 MT, ~30% share). Punjab — 2nd largest by output but #1 in YIELD per hectare. MP — 3rd. Together UP+Punjab+Haryana+MP make ~75% of national wheat production (most rabi). Largest RICE producer — West Bengal (or UP, varies year on year). Largest cotton producer — Maharashtra. Largest sugarcane producer — UP. Largest tea producer — Assam. Largest coffee producer — Karnataka.

questions.stem: MSP (Minimum Support Price) is announced by the Centre on the recommendation of:

options.option_text: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)

questions.explanation: CACP — formed 1965 (then Agricultural Prices Commission, renamed 1985). Statutory body under MoA. Recommends MSPs for 23 crops — 7 cereals (paddy, wheat, maize, ragi, jowar, bajra, barley), 5 pulses, 7 oilseeds, 4 commercial crops (sugarcane FRP, cotton, jute, copra). MSP intended to provide assured income (M.S. Swaminathan formula MSP = C2 + 50% margin — ie cost + 50%). Paddy + wheat have most active procurement (FCI). M.S. Swaminathan is called 'Father of Green Revolution in India' (received Bharat Ratna posthumously, 2024).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The 'Green Revolution' in India during the late 1960s primarily focused on:

options.option_text: High-Yielding Variety (HYV) wheat and rice — particularly in Punjab, Haryana, western UP

questions.explanation: Green Revolution — late 1960s, led by M.S. Swaminathan (Indian) + Norman Borlaug (American, Nobel Peace 1970). Imported HYV wheat (Mexican dwarf varieties — Sonora 64, Lerma Rojo) + rice (IR-8 from Philippines). Combined with assured irrigation, fertilisers, pesticides, MSP, FCI procurement — transformed India from food-deficient (1965-66 famine fears) to self-sufficient by 1975. Focus on Punjab-Haryana-W.UP because of irrigation infrastructure. Side effects — soil exhaustion, water-table depletion, pesticide use, regional inequality.

questions.stem: India's 'White Revolution' (Operation Flood) — making India the largest milk producer globally — was launched by:

options.option_text: Verghese Kurien (under National Dairy Development Board)

questions.explanation: Verghese Kurien — 'Father of White Revolution'. Operation Flood launched 1970 by NDDB, Anand, Gujarat (HQ of Amul). Created a national milk grid linking producers across India to consumers in cities; cooperative dairy model based on Amul (Anand Milk Union Limited). India became #1 milk producer 1998; current ~22% of global milk output. Bharat Ratna posthumously to Kurien (in pipeline; not yet conferred). His birthday 26 November is National Milk Day. Operation Flood often called 'world's largest dairy development programme'.

questions.stem: India's 'Pink Revolution' refers to the rapid growth in:

options.option_text: Meat (especially poultry / pork) and processed-meat exports

questions.explanation: Multiple 'colour revolutions' in India. WHITE — milk; YELLOW — oilseeds; BLUE — fisheries / aquaculture; GREEN — food grains; PINK — meat (also onion / shrimp in some sources); GOLDEN — fruits / honey; SILVER — eggs / cotton; GREY — fertilisers; ROUND — potatoes; BROWN — cocoa / leather. India is now the largest exporter of buffalo meat. The 'Rainbow Revolution' is the umbrella term for pursuing all these together — agricultural diversification.

questions.stem: PM-KISAN scheme provides direct cash transfer to farmers of:
questions.explanation: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi) — launched 24 February 2019. ₹6,000/year via DBT to all eligible landholding farmer families, in 3 four-monthly installments of ₹2,000. Earlier ceiling of 2 hectares removed in June 2019. Excluded: institutional landowners, current/former MPs/MLAs/ministers, professionals (doctors, CAs etc), pension >₹10,000/month. ~10 crore farmers receive benefits. ₹3+ lakh crore transferred since launch.
